image_description: Two men in outdoor gear holding a very large sturgeon horizontally above water. The background shows a blue sky with clouds and distant hills. The fish is the central subject, displaying its elongated body, scutes, and tail.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but the angle and resolution obscure the ventral mouth structure; it appears somewhat blunt rather than distinctly elongated with a clear ventral mouth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the snout where barbels would be located is not visible due to the angle of the fish and the holder's hand/glove obscuring the area.
The snout is clearly pointed and elongated, consistent with sturgeon morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is extremely long and fusiform, spanning the width of the image, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of bony plates (scutes) are clearly visible along the lateral line and dorsal ridge.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is grayish-brown, and the belly area visible near the tail and head is lighter/whitish.
The tail fin is clearly visible on the right side and exhibits the characteristic asymmetry (upper lobe larger than lower lobe) of a heterocercal tail.
